name: Black Kyanite
physical: Traditionally associated with a steady, anchored feeling
Said to bring a sense of stability
Crystal healers link it with relief from tension
summary: Black Kyanite grows in fan-shaped blades, a protective and grounding stone in crystal lore for clearing energy, setting boundaries and staying centred.
intro: Black kyanite is the dark, opaque form of kyanite, most often sold as striking fan-shaped bundles of flat blades that resemble a witch's broom or a bird's wing. The colour comes from graphite and other fine inclusions, giving the stone a matte black to charcoal appearance, sometimes with silvery streaks. Each blade is brittle but beautiful, with parallel grooves along its length. Large fans from Brazil and India are popular as decorative pieces, while polished wands are used in energy work. Compared with blue kyanite, black kyanite is considered a more earthy, protective cousin, ideal for desks and doorways.
history: Black kyanite has no long recorded history of its own, but it belongs to the kyanite family named by Abraham Werner in 1789, from the Greek kyanos for blue. The black fans became popular in the crystal community in the early 2000s, when material from Brazil and India began to appear widely. Lapidaries found that the blades could be shaped into wands and flat pieces, while the fan-shaped bundles were sold in their natural form. Because kyanite was long used as an industrial refractory material, quarrying has been steady, and decorative black pieces are a by-product of that trade.
meaning: Crystal practitioners regard black kyanite as a protective, grounding stone. It is linked with the root and earth star chakras and said to clear unwanted energy, set clear personal boundaries and keep a person steady during hectic times. Like blue kyanite, it is traditionally said never to hold negativity and to be self-cleansing, so it is often placed near other crystals to keep a collection tidy. The fan shape makes it a favourite for sweeping a space or aura in ritual cleansing. Many people place it by the front door or at a desk to keep a workspace calm. Physically it is traditionally associated with a settled feeling, as a symbolic companion only.
howToUse: Place a black kyanite fan near your front door or desk to encourage a protected, tidy atmosphere. Hold a blade in meditation and imagine its dark colour drawing tension down through your body into the ground. Use a wand to sweep gently around your body or room in a clearing ritual, keeping a distance of a few centimetres. Put a piece beside your bed or computer if you feel scattered. Combine with black tourmaline and smoky quartz for strong protective grids.
care: Black kyanite is brittle and easily scratched or snapped along the blade, so handle gently. Avoid soaking, steam and ultrasonic cleaners, which can damage the layers. Wipe with a soft dry cloth. Traditionally it needs little cleansing, though smoke or sound are gentle options. Sun is generally fine. Store fans upright in padded containers, away from harder minerals, and keep thin edges away from children and pets.
identify: Black kyanite appears as flat, opaque, parallel blades, often in fan shapes, with a dull to silky shine and fine lengthwise grooves. Look-alikes include black tourmaline, hornblende, black actinolite, hematite and graphite schist. Black tourmaline has triangular striated crystals and is harder and heavier. Kyanite can be scratched with a steel point lengthwise. Polished wands are sometimes dyed or stabilised, so ask a seller about treatments.

faq.q: What is black kyanite used for?
faq.a: In crystal tradition it is used for protection, grounding and boundary-setting. People keep it near doors and desks, or use blades and wands to sweep a space during energy-clearing rituals.
Tradition says black kyanite is self-cleansing and does not hold negativity, so it is often used to clear other stones. A gentle smoke or sound clear is optional if you wish.

faq.q: Is black kyanite the same as black tourmaline?
faq.a: No. Black kyanite forms flat, brittle blades often in fans, while black tourmaline forms striated triangular prisms. Tourmaline is harder and heavier, and the two are different minerals.
